title: Distribution Reward partners are screened on mission alignment first, not just commercial reach
content:
A.6.1.1.4.3.2.1 sets Skybase's Distribution Reward strategy as encouraging "broad adoption of USDS by bridging into new communities and DeFi platforms," and requires that "prospective partners should demonstrate strong alignment with Skybase's mission."

The four guiding criteria are ordered, and the order is the argument. **Shared Mission Alignment** comes first: partners "must demonstrate a commitment to promoting user-friendly stablecoin usage and responsible financial empowerment." Only then come **Clear Synergy** (a unique distribution channel or robust incentive model), **Community Benefit** (tangible advantages that resonate with Sky's user base), and **Scalability & Compliance** (capacity to handle demand and adherence to "the risk management guidelines described in the Atlas").

This is the Atlas's alignment doctrine reaching commercial counterparty selection. A partner with enormous reach but no commitment to responsible usage fails the first criterion regardless of how much USDS demand it could generate — which is a real cost, since reach is exactly what a distribution program is buying.

The criteria are also the closest thing the primitive has to a rejection standard. Because prospective Instances are published at `Planning` status with named counterparties, these four tests are the public basis on which a pipeline entry can be defended or challenged before it becomes Active.

The last criterion quietly imports external constraint: adherence to Atlas risk management guidelines makes a partner's compliance posture a Skybase problem, so a distribution deal can fail on risk grounds decided elsewhere in the framework.
description: Four stated criteria — Shared Mission Alignment, Clear Synergy, Community Benefit, Scalability & Compliance — make alignment a gating condition for a commercial partnership.
